business_summary.text: HEG Advanced Materials Ltd is a manufacturer of graphite electrodes used in electric arc furnace steelmaking, with operations in hydro power, advanced battery materials, battery energy storage and green power generation through its subsidiaries and associate.

call_points.text: Expansion to 115,000 tons capacity is progressing as planned and targets completion by early 2028.
Uncommitted orders are being offered at higher prices across regions to offset freight and energy costs.
Needle coke prices and shipments are contractually covered until June, protecting costs through September.
TACC anode plant pilot sampling with global OEMs is going well, targeting 40-60% capacity utilization in year one.
Middle East accounts for 20% of annual sales; orders face temporary shipment delays due to regional conflict.
NCLT approval for the composite scheme of arrangement is expected in Q2 FY27.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Erronous demand raised by Electrical Consumer Grievances Redressal forum (ECGRF) for which the amount of Rs. 101.31 Crore was shown as Contingent Liability in the books of Accounts of the Company. The Case has been settled by ECGRF in Company's favour however department has gone to Hon'ble High Court for appeal against the order of ECGRF. The matter is pending with the High Court. After ECGRF ruled in HEG's favor, the provision made in the books was reversed.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Electrical Consumer Grievances Redressal forum (ECGRF), Bhopal
tax_litigation.status: This case relates to a dispute in relation to HEG's electricity bills for the period between June 2005 to October 2011, which has been ongoing, with multiple court hearings and subsequent stays. In February 2023, DISCOM, Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh) raised a demand of INR 78.16 crore in this regard. Pursuant to protest by HEG on the demand, the same was reviewed by DISCOM and INR 26.35 crore was dropped. HEG paid the balance amount of INR 51.81 crore under protest and filed a petition in Jabalpur High Court in May 2023. DISCOM, Bhopal then took the issue to the Electrical Consumer Grievances Redressal Forum (“ECGRF”), which issued a stay on the extra charges. The case was moved from the High Court to the ECGRF and after several hearings with ECGRF, the matter was settled in HEG's favor in February 2024. However, the DISCOM, Bhopal has challenged this order in the High Court. The matter is still pending with Jabalpur High Court.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Disallowance u/s 80 IA & Sec 14A Notice u/s 153A rws 144C (Demand of Rs. 20.18 Crores). Matter is pending before the authority
tax_litigation.status: This case has been merged with the case which is mentioned at Sr. No. 3.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Disallowance u/s 80 IA and Sec 14A Notice u/s 153A rws 144C (Demand of Rs. 19.85 Crores). Matter is pending before the authority
tax_litigation.status: This case is related to AY 2018-19. The original order passed u/s 143(3) of the Income Tax Act, 1961 (“ITA”) dated 02.11.2021, wherein there was a disallowance of deduction u/s 80IA of ITA amounting to INR 19.86 crore on account of reduction in fair value of electricity generated from Captive Power Plant (CPP), disallowance of deduction claimed u/s 35(2AB) on account of Research & Development of INR 0.84 crore and disallowance u/s 14A on account of expenditure in relation to exempt income of INR 0.01 crore. HEG has filed an appeal against demands of this order in CIT (Appeal), Delhi. As on date, the matter is pending before Commissioner of Income-Tax (Appeals) Delhi.

guidance.statement: EBITDA margin guided at 17-18% for Q1 & Q2 FY27 and >20% for full year FY27

operating_notes.text: Management noted pricing pressure on graphite electrodes due to exports from China.
Q4 EBITDA was negatively impacted by a ₹126 Cr fair value loss on GrafTech investment.
Sales volume in FY26 increased by 20% YoY.
Annual sales to Middle East and MENA region account for ~20% of total volume.
Needle coke costs protected until September 2026 via existing purchase commitments.
TACC Limited is developing a 20,000 MT anode materials plant and a 4,000+ tonne graphene derivatives facility.
Graphite segment revenue was ₹677.65 Cr in Q1FY27, 99.5% of consolidated revenue.
Graphite segment results were ₹149.64 Cr in Q1FY27 versus ₹15.39 Cr in Q4FY26.
Share of profit from associate Bhilwara Energy Limited was ₹30.50 Cr in Q1FY27.
US preliminary countervailing duty on HEG's large diameter graphite electrodes set at 6.99%, with cash deposits possibly required on US imports.
Income Tax officials visited HEG's corporate office from 10 to 13 August 2026 to check books of accounts; no demand or finding was disclosed.
Post-scheme HEG Graphite holds ₹4,329.30 Cr of assets and ₹1,309.63 Cr revenue (Sep-2025 proforma); residual HEG holds ₹1,727.48 Cr assets and ₹1,104.69 Cr revenue.
PwC valued the graphite business at ₹393.4 per share and post-demerger HEG at ₹124.0; Bhilwara Energy at ₹141.8 and HEG post-amalgamation at ₹124.0.
Post-scheme HEG will have 32,97,98,912 shares with promoter holding at 60.72%; HEG Graphite will have 19,29,77,530 shares with promoter holding at 56.28%.
Company renamed HEG Advanced Materials Limited from HEG Limited; CIN L23109MP1972PLC008290 unchanged, originally incorporated as Hindustan Electro Graphites Limited.

Salil Bawa, President - Investor Relation (titled President - Corporate Development & Investor Relation in the acceptance letter), resigned effective 14 September 2026; no reason or successor disclosed.

Post-scheme promoter group holds 200,268,011 shares (60.72%); LNJ Spark Advisory LLP holds 40,536,893 shares (12.29%), Redrose Vanijya LLP 93,649,752 (28.40%), Norbury Investments 26,814,955 (8.13%), Microlight Investments 23,327,895 (7.07%
Replus Engitech Private Limited (subsidiary) won ₹217.56 Cr (incl. GST) of lithium-ion battery bank supply orders from Indus Towers, execution by 31 March 2027.
Revised disclosure confirms the Replus Engitech–Indus Towers lithium-ion battery bank order at Rs. 217.56 Crore inclusive of GST, execution on or before 31 March 2027.
LNJ Spark Advisory LLP holds 40,536,893 shares (12.29%) in HEG Advanced Materials Ltd post-scheme allotment
For capital-gains purposes, 27.60% of the pre-demerger cost of acquisition is allocated to HEG Advanced Materials shares and 72.40% to HEG Graphite shares.
Replus Engitech MoU with Indus Towers contemplates 1.5 GWh of dedicated BESS capacity over two years; Replus has deployed over 1 GWh of storage to date.
GST authority dropped FY 2020-21 proceedings under Section 74 of MPGST/CGST Act that had proposed IGST refund recovery plus penalty of ₹1,282.34 Cr; company reported nil impact.

timeline.summary: HEG Limited scheduled Q4 FY26 earnings conference call with **Mr. Ravi Jhunjhunwala (CMD & CEO)**, **Mr. Riju Jhunjhunwala (Vice Chairman)**, and others on **4 May 2026 at 14:00 IST** via 360 ONE Capital.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹603.21 Cr, net loss ₹113.77 Cr (against a loss of ₹73.67 Cr a year earlier).
HEG Advanced Materials reported a Q4FY26 net loss of ₹113.77 Cr, impacted by a ₹126 Cr fair value loss on its GrafTech investment.
Vivek Chaudhary shared the Q4 FY26 earnings conference call recording link on May 4, 2026, at 14:00 hrs IST.
HEG Advanced Materials equity shareholders approved the composite scheme of arrangement with HEG Graphite and Bhilwara Energy at an NCLT-convened meeting.
On May 5, 2026, HEG's equity shareholders, secured creditors, and unsecured creditors approved the composite scheme of arrangement with HEG Graphite and Bhilwara Energy.
HEG held its Q4FY26 concall
India Ratings maintained HEG's IND AA- and IND A1+ ratings on Rating Watch with Developing Implications for ₹1,500 Cr bank facilities and ₹100 Cr CP.
HEG subsidiary TACC signed an MoU with NUS I-FIM to collaborate on advanced functional materials and graphene R&D.

HEG reported Q1FY27 consolidated revenue of ₹680.79 Cr (+10.4% YoY) and PAT of ₹122.34 Cr (+16.7% YoY), with EBITDA margin at 22.12%, and noted MCA reservation of the name HEG Advanced Materials Limited.
2026-07-28: US Department of Commerce set a preliminary 6.99% countervailing duty on HEG's large diameter graphite electrodes, with final CVD and anti-dumping determinations due December 8, 2026.
HEG Advanced Materials Ltd held its 54th AGM on July 29, 2026, approving financial statements, final dividend of Rs.3.40 per share, and re-appointment of Shri Manish Gulati.
HEG Advanced Materials Ltd’s 54th AGM on July 29, 2026, passed all five resolutions, including audited financial statements for FY2026, with 100% shareholder approval via e-voting.
HEG Limited’s 54th AGM (29-Jul-2026) adopted FY2025-26 audited financials, declared ₹3.40 dividend, and re-appointed **Manish Gulati** as Executive Director.
Income Tax department officials checked HEG Advanced Materials' books of accounts at the corporate office from 10 to 13 August 2026, with no demand or finding disclosed.

NCLT Indore Bench sanctioned HEG's composite scheme on 13-Aug-2026: graphite business demerges into HEG Graphite (1:1) and Bhilwara Energy merges into HEG (8:7), with HEG to be renamed HEG Greentech Limited.
NCLT Indore Bench approved the composite scheme of arrangement for HEG's demerger into HEG Graphite Limited and amalgamation of Bhilwara Energy Limited into HEG, effective upon RoC filing.
Board approved composite scheme effective Sept 1, 2026; record date Sept 7, 2026 for 1:1 demerger of graphite business and 8:7 amalgamation of Bhilwara Energy

HEG Limited was renamed HEG Advanced Materials Limited with effect from September 2, 2026, after the composite scheme became effective on September 1, 2026 and ROC Gwalior issued the fresh certificate of incorporation.
2026-09-14: Salil Bawa, President - Investor Relation and Senior Management Personnel, resigned effective 14 September 2026, with his notice period waived.
On 12 September 2026, Singularity Equity Fund I and others were allotted 43,070,852 shares (13.04%) in HEG Advanced Materials Ltd pursuant to the composite scheme involving Bhilwara Energy Ltd.
2026-09-18: Promoter group disclosed holding of 60.72% (from 56.28%) after scheme allotment
2026-09-18: Subsidiary Replus Engitech received orders worth ₹217.56 Cr (incl. GST) from Indus Towers for supply of lithium-ion battery banks, to be executed by 31 March 2027.
2026-09-18: HEG re-filed the Replus Engitech order disclosure for ₹217.56 Cr (incl. GST) of lithium-ion battery banks from Indus Towers, correcting only a missing 'Crore' after the amount.
2026-09-15: LNJ Spark Advisory LLP disclosed acquisition of 40,536,893 shares in HEG Advanced Materials Ltd pursuant to scheme allotment

2026-09-29: HEG Advanced Materials issued tax guidance apportioning 27.60% of pre-demerger share cost to itself and 72.40% to HEG Graphite, following the NCLT order of 13 August 2026 and the 11 September 2026 allotment.
2026-09-30: Replus Engitech signed a non-binding MoU with Indus Towers to explore telecom BESS collaboration, intending 1.5 GWh of dedicated capacity over two years.
2026-10-01: Replus Engitech Private Limited received orders from Indus Towers for supply of lithium-ion battery banks worth ₹127.35 Cr inclusive of GST, to be executed by May 31, 2027
2026-10-12: Company name changed from HEG Graphite Limited to HEG Limited following ROC approval.
2026-10-15: GST authority dropped Section 74 proceedings for FY 2020-21 that had proposed IGST refund recovery and penalty of ₹1,282.34 Cr; company reported nil financial impact.
